On June 24, 2026, UCL Rocket carried out a static hot-fire test campaign for a 7 kN LOX / IPA liquid rocket engine. At the center of this campaign was an Eplus3D-printed CuCrZr combustion chamber designed with 57 internal cooling channels for regenerative thermal management.

During pre-test inspection, the team discovered that approximately 33% of the active coolant channel area was obstructed by metallic swarf generated during the final subtractive post-machining phase. This unforeseen issue was not part of the original test objectives.

In addition, the Eplus3D CuCrZr combustion chamber remained intact after testing, with no visible signs of thermal erosion or structural deformation. Although the coolant channel obstruction was not part of the intended test scope, the chamber’s condition after testing provided further confidence in the material quality, print integrity, and structural resilience of the component.
